title: Kenyan Lemon Tart
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Lemon Tart — a buttery sweet pastry shell filled with a silky, tart lemon curd baked until just set, dusted with icing sugar and blowtorched for a brulée finish. The classic tart that showcases Kenya's abundant, sharp-flavoured lemons.
longDesc: A properly made lemon tart — the passionfruit version's citrus sibling — is one of the greatest pastry achievements. Kenya's lemons are sharp, fragrant, and perfectly suited to this preparation. The brulée top (or simple icing sugar dusting) adds a textural contrast to the silky filling.
steps: Make and blind bake sweet pastry shell as per KEN283.
Make lemon filling: whisk eggs, yolks, sugar, lemon juice, and zest in a saucepan over medium heat.
Stir constantly until mixture thickens enough to coat a spoon — 8—10 minutes.
Remove from heat. Whisk in cold butter piece by piece.
Bake at 160°C for 15—18 minutes until just set with a slight wobble.
Dust with icing sugar before serving, or blowtorch for a brulée effect.
chefTips: Cook the curd over medium-low heat — high heat scrambles the eggs.
A slight wobble is right — it sets fully during refrigeration.
The brulée finish requires a blowtorch — icing sugar is the home alternative.
commonMistakes: Scrambled egg curd — too high heat.
Over-baking in the shell — too firm.
cookingScience: Lemon curd sets through the same protein coagulation as crème pâtissière — egg proteins set between 60—85°C. The high acid content of lemon juice speeds coagulation (acid destabilises egg proteins at lower temperatures) and prevents curdling by creating a more acidic environment that promotes gradual protein network formation.
sustainabilityTips: Kenyan lemons from the coast and Rift Valley — locally produced.
healthBenefits: Lemon is very high in vitamin C.
culturalNote: The Kenyan lemon tart demonstrates the depth of pastry skill in Nairobi's finest bakeries — a technically demanding classic executed with precision, using Kenya's abundant, sharp lemons to produce a dessert of international standard.
